create.title: Coupled alpha high-pass packet and zero-mass BV obstruction
create.statement_tex: Let lambda=mu+nu and m_lambda(beta)=(1-psi(beta))psi(beta+lambda). Its inverse Fourier kernel K_lambda is Schwartz and has zero mass, giving an exact scalar log-dilation commutator. If supp psi is contained in [-M,M] and |lambda|>2M, then m_lambda(beta)=psi(beta+lambda) on all beta, so K_lambda is a modulation of the fixed low-pass kernel and has fixed nonzero L1 norm. A lattice atom retains this packet mass, a hard floor or product-star step retains fixed variation, and N sufficiently separated jumps retain order-N response. Thus zero mass, vanishing moments, or packetwise BV alone supplies no X or height saving. Finite connectors only redistribute a row trace unless the complete signed row response is proved to cancel. This is a scoped no-go, not a lower bound for the fully recombined signed alpha operator.
create.next_action: Build the complete signed incidence table at each actual floor, star, profile, and radial seam; prove cancellation of its singular jump coefficient or isolate the first survivor.

update.statement_tex: Put A=s-z/2 and B=s+z/2. The alpha factor X_zeta(A)zeta(A)L(1-B,chi_4) has unsigned high coefficients and the exact residue-sensitive masked cosine-comb reduction. With lambda=mu+nu, its coupled mask multiplier is m_lambda(beta)=(1-psi(beta))psi(beta+lambda). Although the inverse kernel has zero mass, on separated bounded-alpha slices it is merely a modulation of the fixed low-pass kernel with fixed L1 norm; lattice atoms and floor/star jumps receive no packetwise BV gain. Prove that the complete common-antecedent signed jump response from terminal, A-strip connector, u/v faces, axes, connector axes, mixed connector, corner, top Plemelj, radial R1, profiles, floors, stars, and endpoints cancels or is O_epsilon(X^epsilon), and prove the joint outside-height Cauchy limit. The theorem must overcome normalized X^(1/8+o(1)) and height U^(c'-1/2-Re z/2) capacities. Pure-comb, zero-mass/BV, automatic connector cancellation, uniform radial IBP, side-free, and all-absolute routes are invalid substitutes.
update.next_action: Freeze one actual floor/star/profile/radial seam and derive the full signed terminal-connector-face-axis-corner-Plemelj incidence coefficient; prove exact cancellation or quantify its first survivor before attempting the global height tail.

reject.reason: For |mu+nu| beyond twice the alpha-mask support, the high-pass factor is identically one on the bounded-alpha packet. Its inverse kernel has zero mass but fixed nonzero L1 norm, so atoms and jumps receive no packetwise saving.

Finite Cauchy-Pompeiu and outside-axis connectors are rowwise contour identities that redistribute a jump trace. Cancellation requires the complete signed row response to vanish, which is not an accepted identity.

The high-pass preserves the singular jump atom before smoothing, and the bounded-alpha packet gives fixed total variation per hard floor or product-star jump. N separated jumps retain order-N capacity.

no_change.reason: The alpha signed seam response and outside-height limit remain open.
Round 50 rejects a scalar proof route but provides no alpha estimate.
The alpha transition estimate and other M1 interfaces remain open.
No unconditional Gauss-circle estimate is claimed.

round_assessment.reason: Round 50 rigorously rejects the zero-mass shortcut, identifies the exact moving packet, and narrows the next target to signed jump-trace incidence. One discovery task produced no artifact, so evidence is strong for the no-go but not for a positive complete-operator formula.
